chunks: Say the ‘aṣr (afternoon) prayers with them when the sun is still shining in a portion of the day enough for covering the distance of two farsakhs (about six miles).

key_terms.بَيْضَاءُ: White/bright (referring to the sun's brightness before setting)
key_terms.فَرْسَخَانِ: Two farsakhs (a unit of distance, approx. 6 miles)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific time limit for performing the ‘aṣr prayer according to this narration?
ai.summary: This narration from *Nahj al-Balagha* offers a practical, time-based definition of the 'aṣr prayer window, emphasizing the urgency of performing it before the sun's brightness diminishes significantly. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on adhering to the specific temporal boundaries (*awqāt*) of prayers to ensure they are offered within their prescribed times, rather than merely at the onset of the time. The reference to traveling two *farsakhs* provides a tangible metric for the remaining daylight, underscoring the importance of timely devotion in daily governance and personal practice.
